Stop work and go immediately to the designated assembly point
Continue working until you see smoke or a fire marshal tells you to move

bank.question: When should an accident or near miss be reported to your supervisor?
bank.explanation: You must report all accidents, including 'near misses', to ensure steps can be taken to prevent a more serious accident in the future
options: Only if someone was seriously injured
Every time, even if nobody was hurt (a near miss)
Only if the accident caused damage to expensive equipment
Only if you think it was someone else's fault

bank.question: Site management should monitor controls rather than assuming they remain effective
bank.explanation: This is true because inspection and supervision confirm whether controls are being used and still work.

bank.question: You only need to record an accident in the accident book if the injury is serious enough to require a hospital visit
bank.explanation: This is false because all accidents that require first aid must be recorded in the accident book, no matter how minor they seem

bank.question: When assessing manual handling, what does the acronym 'TILE' stand for?
bank.explanation: Manual handling assessments must consider the task, the individual's capability, the load, and the environment (TILE)
options: Time, Individual, Language, Effort
Tools, Injury, Location, Equipment
Task, Individual, Load, Environment
Technique, Interest, Level, Energy

bank.question: What is the most common type of health problem caused by poor manual handling techniques?
bank.explanation: Manual handling is one of the leading causes of back pain and musculoskeletal injuries in the construction industry
options: Back injuries and muscle strains
Hearing loss and tinnitus
Lung disease and breathing problems
Vibration white finger

bank.question: If you see a small oil spill on the ground and it is not your job to clean it, you can leave it and walk past
bank.explanation: This is false because even if it is not your job to clean up, you have a duty of care to report the spill or clear it if safe to do so to prevent others from slipping

bank.question: What is the main rule for using a ladder to work at height?
bank.explanation: Ladders should only be used for low-risk, short-duration tasks (lasting less than 30 minutes) where three points of contact can be maintained
options: As a permanent way to reach a scaffold platform
For short-duration, low-risk work only
To carry heavy loads up to a roof
Only if no other equipment is available on site

bank.question: How is a worker most likely to catch Leptospirosis (Weil's disease)?
bank.explanation: Leptospirosis (Weil's disease) is a serious infection carried in the urine of rats and is often found in contaminated water or damp soil
options: Coming into contact with old bird droppings
Inhaling dust from cutting old concrete blocks
Touching lead-based paint without using gloves
Contact with water or soil contaminated by rat urine

bank.question: An HSE inspector can stop work on a site immediately if they believe the activity is dangerous
bank.explanation: This is true because the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) can issue a Prohibition Notice which stops specific work activities immediately if they pose a risk of serious personal injury

bank.question: What is the main purpose of a site induction?
bank.explanation: The primary purpose of a site induction is to explain the specific safety rules and emergency procedures for that particular site
options: To check your trade qualifications
To explain the site's specific safety rules and hazards
To give you your weekly work schedule
To introduce you to the client's family

bank.question: If a Health and Safety Executive (HSE) inspector issues a 'prohibition notice' on a piece of equipment, what does it mean?
bank.explanation: HSE inspectors have the power to stop work immediately if they believe there is a risk of serious personal injury
options: Wait until the end of the shift to stop work
Finish the current task before stopping
Stop work immediately and follow the inspector's instructions
Ask the site manager for permission to continue

bank.question: What should be used to locate underground power cables before you start digging?
bank.explanation: Underground services should be identified using cable avoidance tools (CAT) and signal generators (Genny) before any digging starts
options: A cable avoidance tool (CAT) and a signal generator (Genny) suspecting buried services
A pickaxe to carefully break the surface and see what is underneath
A metal detector used for finding coins or archaeological finds
A site map that is at least five years old

bank.question: What is the main reason for wearing high-visibility (hi-vis) clothing on site?
bank.explanation: High-visibility clothing ensures that plant operators and vehicle drivers can see you, especially in low light or busy areas
options: To keep your clothes clean while working
To ensure vehicle and plant operators can see you
To show which company you work for
To protect you from chemical spills

bank.question: Reporting a 'near miss' can help prevent a more serious accident from happening in the future
bank.explanation: This is true because near misses are essential indicators of potential hazards; reporting them allows the site to fix issues before an actual injury occurs

bank.question: When a fire alarm sounds, it is acceptable to finish the task you are doing before evacuating the site
bank.explanation: This is false because if a fire alarm sounds, you must stop work immediately and go to the designated assembly point; you should never stay behind to finish a task

bank.question: Who has the overall responsibility for managing health and safety on a construction site?
bank.explanation: The principal contractor is responsible for the overall safety and coordination of the entire construction site
options: The health and safety inspector
The principal contractor
The local council's building control officer
The first-aider on the site

bank.question: If a qualified person is unavailable, a general site worker can move a mobile tower scaffold even if they haven't been trained
bank.explanation: This is false because if a specialist task is required, you must wait for a trained and competent person to perform it to avoid accidents

bank.question: Why is it important to wear hearing protection in noisy environments?
bank.explanation: Noise is more than just a nuisance; it can cause permanent, irreversible hearing loss
options: It can cause permanent hearing loss
It makes you more tired at the end of the day
It causes a temporary headache only
It has no long-term health effects

bank.question: Which animal is the most common carrier of Weil's disease (Leptospirosis) on site?
bank.explanation: Leptospirosis (Weil's disease) is a serious infection spread in the urine of animals, most commonly rats
options: Pigeons
Domestic cats
Foxes
Rats

bank.question: Ladders are the preferred piece of equipment for long-duration tasks involving heavy materials at height
bank.explanation: This is false because ladders should primarily be used for access or for short-duration light work (usually no more than 30 minutes)

bank.question: When must basic welfare facilities (toilets, washing, etc.) be available on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Welfare facilities, including toilets and washing areas, must be provided from the very first day on site for all workers
options: Only when more than 10 people are working on site
Within one week of starting the project
Only if the project lasts longer than 30 days
From the very first day the work starts

bank.question: According to the hierarchy of control, PPE is the last line of defence against a hazard
bank.explanation: This is true because while personal protective equipment (PPE) is important, it is the 'last resort' and should only be used if the risk cannot be removed or reduced in other ways

bank.question: What type of fire extinguisher is specifically designed for use on deep-fat fryer fires?
bank.explanation: A class F fire involves cooking oils and fats; it requires a specialized wet chemical extinguisher
options: A Water extinguisher
A Powder extinguisher
A Wet Chemical extinguisher
A CO2 extinguisher

bank.question: How can manual handling training help you on site?
bank.explanation: Manual handling training teaches you how to assess risks and use correct techniques to prevent long-term musculoskeletal injuries
options: Work much faster than other people
Understand the risks and lift more safely
Lift any weight regardless of how heavy it is
Avoid all physical work on site

bank.question: Which health condition is most commonly associated with frequent contact with wet cement or mortar?
bank.explanation: Skin contact with wet concrete or mortar can cause irritant or allergic dermatitis due to its high alkalinity
options: Tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
Leptospirosis (Weil's disease)
Asbestosis
Dermatitis and skin burns

bank.question: It is acceptable to use a step ladder as a work platform for a task that takes a full day to complete
bank.explanation: This is false because step ladders are intended for short-duration light work. If the task lasts for hours, a safer platform like a tower scaffold or podium should be used

bank.question: Mental health and fatigue can affect safety decisions on site
bank.explanation: This is true because tired or distressed workers may be more likely to make errors or miss hazards.

bank.question: What is the main reason for using 110V electricity instead of 230V on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Power tools are usually 110V (yellow) on site to reduce the risk of a fatal electric shock compared to 230V
options: The cable is easier to see on the floor
110V tools are more powerful than 230V tools
The risk of a fatal electric shock is greatly reduced
The electricity is cheaper for the contractor to run

bank.question: What does a safety sign that is triangular with a yellow background and black border mean?
bank.explanation: A triangular sign with a yellow background and a black border is a warning sign, alerting you to a specific hazard
options: A mandatory requirement (must do)
A warning of a specific danger or hazard
A prohibition (must not do)
The location of emergency first-aid equipment

bank.question: Which animal is most commonly associated with the spread of Weil's disease (Leptospirosis)?
bank.explanation: Rats carry Leptospirosis (Weil's disease) in their urine, which can contaminate water and wet ground on construction sites
options: Rats
Pigeons
Foxes
Badgers

bank.question: If you encounter a material you think might be asbestos, what is the first action you should take?
bank.explanation: You must stop work and report it immediately so the material can be identified and made safe by specialists
options: Break it up and put it in a skip
Cover it with soil or sand
Seal it with duct tape and continue working
Stop work and report it to your supervisor immediately

bank.question: Are you allowed to use a piece of plant or machinery if you have not been trained to use it?
bank.explanation: You must never use equipment that you are not trained and authorized to operate
options: Yes, if you have seen someone else do it
Yes, provided you are careful
No, you must be trained and authorized to use it
No, unless it is an emergency

bank.question: What is the definition of a 'hazard'?
bank.explanation: In the context of health and safety, a hazard is defined as any source or situation with the potential to cause harm or damage
options: The likelihood of an accident happening
Anything that has the potential to cause harm
The severity of an injury after an accident
A specific piece of broken equipment

bank.question: In the 'TILE' manual handling assessment, the letter 'E' stands for the Environment
bank.explanation: This is true because manual handling risk assessments must consider the Task, the Individual, the Load, and the Environment

bank.question: A near miss should be ignored if nobody was actually injured
bank.explanation: This is false because near misses are warning signs and should be reported so the underlying risk can be controlled before harm occurs.

bank.question: What should you do if you think a job you are doing is dangerous?
bank.explanation: You must stop work immediately if you encounter any situation that is dangerous to yourself or others
options: Wait until the end of your shift to report it
Carry on but try to be as careful as possible
Stop work immediately and tell your supervisor
Ask a colleague to finish the job for you

bank.question: What should you receive when you first arrive to work on a new construction site?
bank.explanation: The site induction is a legal requirement where you are briefed on site-specific safety rules and emergency procedures
options: A free lunch provided by the contractor
A test of your trade skills and experience
A meeting to discuss your weekly pay and taxes
Information on the hazards and rules specific to that site

bank.question: Waste chutes and skips should be used in a way that prevents falling materials and exposure to dust
bank.explanation: This is true because waste handling needs controls for impact, dust and manual handling risks.

bank.question: Open edges should be protected by suitable guardrails or equivalent fall-prevention measures
bank.explanation: This is true because collective edge protection reduces the risk of falls for everyone working nearby.

bank.question: An HSE inspector has the legal right to seize and remove any equipment they believe is dangerous or has been involved in an accident
bank.explanation: This is true because the HSE has the legal authority to seize and examine any equipment or materials that they believe may have caused an accident

bank.question: Safety helmets have an indefinite lifespan and only need to be replaced if they show visible signs of a crack
bank.explanation: This is false because modern safety helmets are made of plastic that degrades over time and from UV exposure; they should be replaced according to the manufacturer's date

bank.question: At what height must edge protection (such as guard rails) be provided on a working platform?
bank.explanation: Handrails or edge protection must be installed on any edge where a person could fall a distance likely to cause personal injury
options: Only if the fall is over 5 metres
Only if the worker asks for it
Wherever a person could fall a distance likely to cause injury
Only when working on a roof

bank.question: Materials should be stacked so they are stable and do not obstruct access routes
bank.explanation: This is true because unstable or badly located stacks can fall, block escapes or cause trips.

bank.question: Reversing vehicles are safest when pedestrians can freely walk behind them
bank.explanation: This is false because reversing areas should be controlled and pedestrians kept away from vehicle movements.

bank.question: Before entering a deep excavation, what is the most important check you must make?
bank.explanation: You should never enter an unsupported excavation, even a shallow one, as soil can collapse without warning
options: Check for underground services first
Ensure the sides are properly shored or battered back
Wear a safety harness and line
Wait until a second person is standing by the edge
